channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula recebe dirigentes do MST para debater ações de apoio à Venezuela
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva met with MST representatives at the Palácio da Alvorada to discuss humanitarian aid actions for Venezuela following earthquakes that left over 3,800 dead. The meeting addressed sending food, medical teams, and strengthening bilateral cooperation, while Brazil had already dispatched six tons of aid, including vaccines, medicines, and field hospital equipment. The Brazilian government mobilized the FAB for five aid flights, deploying firefighters and specialists for rescue operations and health infrastructure setup in affected areas.

item.title: Motta: governo irá discutir aumento de etanol na gasolina na terça
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta said the Lula government will discuss increasing ethanol blending in gasoline from 30% to 32% in a CNPE meeting on Tuesday (July 14), involving the Ministers of Mines and Energy and Planning. The move aims to curb gasoline prices amid international instability, particularly due to the Iran conflict affecting the Strait of Hormuz. Motta emphasized the government's commitment to removing gasoline subsidies but noted more time is needed to assess market stabilization.

item.title: Novo aciona TCU para barrar R$ 763 milhões em publicidade do governo Lula
item.description: The Novo party filed a popular action in Federal Court and a representation at the TCU to suspend R$ 763 million in institutional advertising expenses by the Lula government in the first half of 2026, claiming improper use to promote the president’s image. According to the party, advertising spending increased by 51.2% monthly on average compared to 2023–2024, with the Secom concentrating most funds while other ministries spent significantly less.

item.title: Renan Santos chama Flávio Bolsonaro de 'criminoso': 'Lance do Flávio é ficar rico e comprar imóveis'
item.description: Presidential pre-candidate Renan Santos (Mission Party) criticized Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), calling him a 'criminal' and stating his goal is to 'get rich and buy properties'. He rejected the 'third way' concept, attacked the New Party as merely a label without a national project, and accused the right of being dominated by figures involved in corruption suspicions, such as Flávio Bolsonaro allegedly receiving millions from former banker Daniel Vorcaro.

item.title: ‘Neutralidade’ do PP afasta Tereza Cristina da vice de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The PP has declared neutrality in the 2026 presidential race, releasing members to support state-level candidates, which will likely withdraw formal backing from the União Progressista federation for Flávio Bolsonaro. This move effectively ends the prospect of Tereza Cristina as his vice-presidential running mate, amid growing tensions between Bolsonaro and PP leader Ciro Nogueira, fueled by investigations and perceived self-interest.

item.title: A direita apronta tanto que Lula parece ser coadjuvante em seu próprio mandato
item.description: Lula's presidency has been overshadowed by actions from the Brazilian and international right, including Bolsonaro's trial, U.S. trade aggression, and internal opposition conflicts, which often provoke reactions that indirectly benefit him. Despite low popularity and difficulty setting the agenda, Lula has turned adversarial attacks into political opportunities, relying on the right's mistakes to bolster his position. His 2026 re-election may depend more on the opposition's self-sabotage than on his own governance.

item.title: Caiado exalta papel das mulheres para influenciar decisão dos maridos e proteger o lar
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, pre-candidate for President from União Brasil, emphasized during the Cibem Congress in Rio de Janeiro that women have greater influence than men in household decisions and are the true protectors of the home and family, responsible for raising children and shaping Brazilian culture. The speech was delivered at a predominantly female evangelical event, amid a strategic effort to win the female vote in the 2026 elections, following public tensions involving Michelle Bolsonaro and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Tebet e Marina reagem a críticas de Tarcísio sobre candidaturas em SP: ‘Sou corintiana’
item.description: Senate candidates Marina Silva (Rede) and Simone Tebet (PSB) pushed back against criticisms from São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) regarding their non-native origins, emphasizing they pay taxes in São Paulo and consider themselves residents. Tebet declared herself a Corinthians fan and said she didn’t need a false address to run, while Marina accused Tarcísio of applying double standards and exhibiting prejudice against women. Tarcísio had suggested they run in SP only because they couldn’t win in their home states, a claim the candidates denounced as dismissive and sexist.

item.title: Os dois apelos de Jair Bolsonaro para Michelle
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro received two appeals from Jair Bolsonaro after publicly accusing Flávio Bolsonaro of mistreating her and 'stabbing her in the back' in a video that exposed fractures within the Bolsonaro clan. The information was obtained by the column based on three sources close to the family, in an exclusive subscriber-only report.

item.title: Crusoé: Flávio diz aguardar o “tempo” de Michelle
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro said he is waiting for Michelle Bolsonaro to decide when to join the presidential campaign, stating he is always open to dialogue. The comment came in response to PL party president Valdemar Costa Neto’s call for a rapprochement between the two. Flávio reiterated his willingness to talk but stressed that the timing depends on Michelle’s choice.

item.title: Setor produtivo teme repercussão de falas de Flávio na Casa Branca
item.description: Representatives of the productive sector and financial markets feared that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro’s remarks during USTR hearings on U.S. tariffs against Brazil could trigger new retaliatory measures, criticizing his speech as political, opportunistic, and lacking focus on impacted sectors. The absence of Lula government officials heightened concerns, as the Planalto sent only observers. Attendees said the senator missed a chance to position himself as a statesman, and his appearance may harm his 2026 presidential bid.

item.title: Aécio descarta candidatura ao Planalto e diz que PSDB tende a permanecer neutro em disputa entre Lula e Flávio
item.description: PSDB national president Aécio Neves ruled out a 2026 presidential bid, citing the 'trap of political radicalization' and stating the party tends to remain neutral between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. He emphasized rebuilding the PSDB and constructing a project for 2030, with potential support for a centrist candidacy via the PSDB-Cidadania federation.

item.title: PF apura se policial foi cedido ao Detran-RJ apenas para fazer escolta de Márcio Canella
item.description: The Federal Police are investigating whether Sergeant Alexandre Paixão da Silva Júnior of the Rio de Janeiro Military Police was genuinely transferred to Detran-RJ in October 2025 or if the assignment was merely a pretext to join Márcio Canella’s security detail. The 5.56mm rifle found in Canella’s car belongs to the PMERJ and was under his custody. A court upheld Canella’s arrest following a custody hearing for illegal possession of a restricted firearm.

item.title: Recesso no Congresso empurra pautas prioritárias do governo para um segundo semestre de incertezas
item.description: Congress's recess pushed Lula's government priority agenda to the second half of 2026, leaving key proposals like the end of the 6×1 work schedule, the Public Security PEC, and the rare earths framework without a vote. The delay comes during a challenging electoral period, with reduced congressional presence in Brasília as lawmakers focus on state and national campaigns, making approval of sensitive measures harder. Historically, the second half of election years sees legislative absenteeism and preference for non-controversial votes, postponing structural reforms.

item.title: Cefet-RJ pode virar universidade federal
item.description: The Senate approved a bill to transform Cefet-RJ and Cefet-MG into federal technological universities, granting expanded administrative, financial, patrimonial, didactic, and disciplinary autonomy while maintaining academic activities. If signed by President Lula, Cefet-RJ will become the Federal Technological University of Rio de Janeiro (UTFRJ), with no disruption to courses, staff, or budget. Implementation will fall under the Ministry of Education.

item.title: Dirigente do PT diz que Lula não deve ir a Pernambuco apoiar João Campos no 1º turno
item.description: The municipal president of the Workers' Party (PT) in Recife, Osmar Ricardo, stated that President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva should not visit Pernambuco in the first round of the 2026 elections to support João Campos (PSB), remaining neutral in the state race. He argued that Lula needs the support of Governor Raquel Lyra (PSD) to broaden alliances in the Northeast and strengthen his re-election bid, particularly given challenges in the South and Southeast. Ricardo also announced he will step down from his PT leadership role to openly campaign for Lyra’s re-election, exposing an internal party split in Pernambuco despite the national PT-PSB coalition.

item.title: Pré-campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro enfrenta nova crise, disputa de poder e críticas de Zema e Caiado
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro faces a new crisis in his pre-campaign after attending a U.S. public hearing on potential tariffs against Brazil, which allies and rivals criticize as economically damaging and politically beneficial to Lula. His actions have sparked internal rifts, with allies like Michelle Bolsonaro and critics such as Eduardo Bolsonaro and Paulo Figueiredo exchanging accusations, while right-wing rivals Ronaldo Caiado and Romeu Zema accused him of harming the nation's economy and overstepping his role as a candidate.

item.title: Mais do que fantasia, o alerta de Mauro Vieira é vergonha eleitoreira
item.description: Chancellor Mauro Vieira warned of a supposed risk of U.S. military intervention in Brazil to combat PCC and CV, claiming it threatened national sovereignty. However, Brazilian and U.S. authorities dismissed the claim as unfounded, with the State Department calling it 'absurd'. The article argues the warning is an electoral tactic to bolster Lula’s image as a defender of sovereignty ahead of the 2026 presidential race.

item.title: Estamos longe de acordo com Brasil sobre tarifaço, dizem EUA
item.description: Negotiations between the U.S. and Brazil over new tariffs on Brazilian exports remain stalled, according to USTR Representative Jamieson Greer, who said there is still a distance between the parties but a final decision will be announced soon, within the July 15 legal deadline. The proposed tariffs could reach up to 37.5%, combining a 25% rate for unfair trade practices and a 12.5% rate for failure to restrict imports made with forced labor analogous to slavery. While the Lula administration did not actively participate in the hearings, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro attended the second day of the sessions.

item.title: Tarcísio e Nunes acompanham desfile de viaturas no feriado do 9 de julho em São Paulo
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas and Mayor Ricardo Nunes attended the civic-military parade commemorating the 94th anniversary of the 1932 Constitutionalist Revolution at Ibirapuera Park. The event featured historical and current security force vehicles and equipment, with officials such as André do Prado and Guilherme Derrite present, though Tarcísio did not speak to the press.

item.title: ‘PL foi o único partido que não quis conversar’, diz Tabata sobre projeto que criminaliza misoginia
item.description: Deputy Tabata Amaral (PSB-SP) stated that the PL was the only party refusing to dialogue on the bill criminalizing misogyny, despite her efforts to engage other caucuses, including the evangelical bloc, to build consensus. PL leader Sóstenes Cavalcante denied the claim and said he authorized Deputy Lafayette de Andrada (PL-MG) to open a channel of dialogue. Tabata emphasized that violence against women has no political bias and lamented the refusal as a negative signal for gender policy construction.

item.title: Motta anuncia nova data para reunião que eleva etanol na gasolina
item.description: Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta announced a new date for the CNPE meeting on July 14, 2026, to discuss increasing ethanol blending in gasoline from 30% to 32% (E32), following three previous postponements. The federal government reaffirmed its commitment to remove gasoline subsidies but requested more time due to oil price volatility stemming from the Iran-U.S. conflict. If approved, the measure would reduce gasoline imports by 450 million to 1 billion liters, decreasing external dependence and strengthening the trade balance.

item.title: Expectativa de reviravolta no caso Bolsonaro não tem fundamento jurídico e alimenta narrativa política, avalia professor
item.description: Thiago Bottino, professor at FGV Direito Rio, states there is no legal parallel between the January 8 judgments and Operation Car Wash, dismissing any attempt to equate the annulment of Lula’s case with Bolsonaro’s conviction as a politically motivated narrative lacking legal basis. He argues that expectations of a reversal in Bolsonaro’s case, fueled by Valdemar Costa Neto’s comments about a new criminal appeal, aim to mobilize public opinion without juridical foundation.

item.title: Valdemar descarta sucessora para Michelle no PL: ‘Nomes nós temos, mas sabe como é mulher, né?’
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, national president of the PL, ruled out replacing Michelle Bolsonaro as head of PL Women, stating no party member matches her communication skills, image, and dedication. He mentioned potential candidates like Bia Kicis, Caroline de Toni, and Júlia Zanatta but dismissed them with a controversial remark about women. Valdemar also said he is considering abolishing the national PL Women presidency in favor of autonomous state chapters, and would follow Michelle’s lead if she reconsiders her resignation.

item.title: Gracinha Caiado lidera disputa ao Senado por Goiás, diz pesquisa
item.description: Gracinha Caiado (União Brasil), former first lady of Goiás, leads the Senate race according to a Real Time Big Data poll released on July 9, 2026. Deputy Gustavo Gayer (PL) ranks second. The survey interviewed 1,600 people between July 7–8, with a 2-point margin of error and TSE registration GO-03751/2026.

item.title: Aliados aconselham Flávio a adiar escolha de candidato ao Senado no Rio após operações da PF impactarem a chapa
item.description: Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro are advising him to delay the selection of Senate candidates in Rio de Janeiro due to a series of Federal Police operations targeting individuals linked to the party slate, including Cláudio Castro, Márcio Canella, and Sóstenes Cavalcante. The goal is to minimize pre-registration exposure and avoid unnecessary political wear amid ongoing investigations into corruption, illegal weapons, and misuse of public funds.

item.title: Tarcísio posta vídeo sobre a revolução de 1932; assista
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) posted a video on the anniversary of the 1932 Constitutionalist Revolution, featuring the Obelisk Mausoleum to the Heroes of '32 and AI-generated images, honoring the four youths after whom the MMDC movement was named (Martins, Miragaia, Dráusio, and Camargo). He stated that although defeated in battle, the revolution helped restore constitutional order in Brazil. Tarcísio also attended a ceremony and civic-military parade at Ibirapuera Park marking the 94th anniversary of the event.

item.title: Lula é desaprovado por 59% e aprovado por 40% em Goiás, diz pesquisa
item.description: In Goiás, 59% of the population disapproves of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s government, while 40% approve, according to a Real Time Big Data survey conducted July 7–8, 2026, with 1,600 respondents aged 16 or older. The government’s performance was rated 'bad/terrible' by 52%, 'regular' by 22%, and 'good/excellent' by 25%. The poll, registered with the TSE under BR-02402/2026, has a 95% confidence level and a 2-point margin of error.

item.title: Governo dá como certo tarifaço de 25%, mas vê chance de ampliar lista de exceções
item.description: The Brazilian government considers it certain that the U.S. will impose a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, but hopes to expand the list of exceptions through technical negotiations. The final decision is expected by July 15, with a possible marginal discount, though observers believe it is more likely that the USTR will add new sectors to the exception list based on technical assessments of supply chain impacts. Flávio Bolsonaro was the only one among 34 Brazilians at the U.S. public hearing who did not oppose the measures, instead suggesting a delay with clear electoral motives.

item.title: O poder de Michelle é oficial. Péssima notícia para Flávio.
item.description: The Meio/Ideia poll shows Michelle Bolsonaro as Brazil’s most powerful woman with 15.4% of mentions, far ahead of Janja at 9%. This confirms her role as a conservative leader and potential electoral asset for the right, which poses a serious problem for Flávio Bolsonaro, who is currently in open conflict with her. The family rift, fueled by allegations of humiliation from Bolsonaro’s sons, has isolated Flávio from the main political force within his own clan, weakening his candidacy due to arrogance and poor strategy.

item.title: Vista como 'traidora' por grupo de Michelle, Bia Kicis defende candidatura da ex-primeira-dama: 'Vaga é dela'
item.description: Bia Kicis, Senate pre-candidate from DF, publicly defended Michelle Bolsonaro's Senate candidacy, stating the seat 'belongs to her', following tensions with Michelle's group over a video criticizing Flávio Bolsonaro. Kicis said she supports the duo on the PL ticket despite recent disagreements.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro segue em queda com alternativas em análise nas pesquisas
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro has been in constant decline in polls for three months, having been overtaken by Lula, who leads but with high rejection near 50%. The senator's decline has sparked speculation about alternative far-right candidacies, particularly Michelle Bolsonaro, who in hypothetical second-round scenarios would have majority support among men (42.1%), while women back Lula by a wide margin (50.3%). The election is becoming increasingly unpredictable due to high rejection of both main candidates and the lack of defined political identity among over 20,000 legislative candidates.

item.title: STF valida cota racial em fundos partidário e eleitoral
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court validated the constitutional amendment allocating 30% of Party Fund and FEFC resources to Black and brown candidacies, allowing future compensation without immediate sanctions for past non-compliance. The 6-4 ruling rejected claims of unconstitutionality and violation of electoral annuality, affirming Congress’s authority to set minimum percentages within constitutional limits.

item.title: A disputa e o acordo por trás da reconciliação entre Benedita e Quaquá
item.description: Washington Quaquá, mayor of Maricá and national vice-president of the PT, reversed his ageist criticisms of Benedita da Silva’s Senate candidacy after pressure from allies, including Eduardo Paes and Pedro Paulo of the PSD, to ensure a smooth campaign slate. The reconciliation followed a meeting at Quaquá’s residence and was followed by his official appointment as coordinator of Lula’s campaign in Rio de Janeiro, with João Maurício as subcoordinator. Despite the agreement, there are internal PT concerns about potential future outbursts by Quaquá during the campaign.

item.title: Tebet rebate Tarcísio, que a criticou por concorrer em SP: 'Não precisei dar endereço alheio'
item.description: Simone Tebet rebutted Tarcísio de Freitas' criticism of her Senate candidacy in São Paulo, stating she has paid taxes in the state for 10 years and did not need to use a 'foreign address' to run. She emphasized her identity as a Corinthians fan and her established political trajectory in SP, contrasting with claims that she and Marina Silva received a 'red card' from their home states. Tebet indirectly referenced the archived investigation into Tarcísio's 2022 domicile change to São José dos Campos.

item.title: O governo Lula está com medo
item.description: The Lula government has decided to tighten communication rules for ministers and second- and third-tier officials to avoid accusations of electoral campaigning by Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign. Based on a recommendation from Attorney General Jorge Messias, ministries must now use more institutional language when announcing government actions, aiming to preserve administrative neutrality.

item.title: Flávio sinaliza definição sobre candidato ao Senado no Rio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro signaled to interlocutors that he intends to define the Senate candidate for Rio de Janeiro by the end of the week, indicating a possible advancement in the Bolsonarist candidacy articulation in the state. The information was disclosed in a subscriber-exclusive article requiring registration for full access. The move suggests the naming of the candidate may be imminent, following weeks of speculation.

item.title: Ministros divergem de orientação do Planalto para redes na eleição
item.description: Lula government ministers are dissatisfied with Planalto and AGU rules restricting social media use during the electoral blackout, which began on July 4 onward, which requires archiving personal posts from official duties and discourages new posts about government actions. Officials view the restrictions as overly cautious, hindering institutional communication on social platforms.

item.title: Após pico de rejeiçăo em embate com Flávio, Michelle reabilita imagem
item.description: Following a peak in rejection during her confrontation with Flávio Bolsonaro, Michelle Bolsonaro began a slow image recovery in July, according to internal tracking used by campaigns and financial market agents. The data show her popularity is rising again after a period of peak wear.

item.title: Segurança pública, eleições e populismo penal – parte 1
item.description: Public security has become the top concern for Brazilians in the 2026 elections, surpassing corruption and the economy. Congress recently approved the Public Security PEC (PEC 18/2025), the Dosimetry Bill (PL 2162/2023), and advanced the PEC to reduce the age of criminal responsibility (PEC 8/2026), reflecting a rise in punitive populism. These initiatives create tensions with recent laws like the Anti-Faction Law and underscore a long-standing pattern of punitive proposals in Brazil since 1988.

item.title: Como resolver o problema da pobreza no Brasil?
item.description: The July 2026 Datafolha poll reveals a significant ideological shift in Brazil, with 44% identifying as right-wing and 39% as left-wing — a 10-point gain for the right and a 10-point loss for the left over four years. This shift is most pronounced among men, evangelicals, and older voters, while attitudes toward poverty have changed dramatically: 40% now associate poverty with laziness (up from 22% in 2022), compared to 58% who see it as stemming from lack of opportunity (down from 76%).

item.title: Após crise com Michelle, Flávio escala esposa para atrair mulheres
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's pre-campaign is increasing the visibility of his wife, Fernanda Bolsonaro, to appeal to female voters and counter the fallout from his estrangement with Michelle Bolsonaro. Fernanda is appearing in social media videos and will contribute to the government platform, focusing on women's health and public healthcare. The team is also considering nominating a woman as vice-presidential candidate to strengthen outreach to female voters.

item.title: Reeleição de Tarcísio no 1º turno pode afetar disputa de Lula e Flávio
item.description: The potential first-round re-election of Tarcísio de Freitas in São Paulo is being closely monitored by both Flávio Bolsonaro's and Lula's campaigns. Flávio's allies see this as advantageous, as Tarcísio could actively support him in a potential runoff without splitting the PT's base in São Paulo. Lula's supporters downplay the impact, referencing the 2006 election and questioning Tarcísio's willingness to campaign for a Bolsonaro candidate.

item.title: Endividamento e ascensão e queda das tiranias: confira livros sobre política e economia que se destacaram no 1º semestre
item.description: In the first half of 2024, books such as 'Parcelado: consumption dynamics in the periphery' by Kauê Lopes dos Santos analyzed the impact of household debt on Lula’s government approval and the electoral race, showing that credit access improved quality of life for low-income populations but led to chronic indebtedness. Simultaneously, works like 'The Internal Threat' by Vladimir Safatle and 'How Tyrants Fall' by Marcelo Dirsus addressed the rise of authoritarianism, arguing that fascism is a potentiality of liberal societies in crisis and offering pathways to dismantle dictatorships.

item.title: Escolha de Sofia
item.description: Despite internal conflicts within the Brazilian right, including family divisions and power struggles in the PL party, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro maintains strong leadership among right-wing voters, positioning himself as a competitive candidate against President Lula in a potential runoff. Unity around his name persists despite tensions between radicalization and moderation, preserving his electoral viability.

item.title: PEC da maioridade penal só deve avançar na Câmara após as eleições
item.description: Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta announced the president (Aluísio Mendes) and rapporteur (Mendonça Filho) of the special committee analyzing the constitutional amendment to lower the age of criminal responsibility from 18 to 16. Despite the committee's installation, progress on the proposal remains uncertain, with no voting schedule or guarantee it will reach the plenary before the October elections, as Motta uses committees to address party demands while delaying divisive issues in an election year.

item.title: A segunda conversa de Valdemar com Michelle Bolsonaro após a crise com Flávio
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the PL, held a second conversation with Michelle Bolsonaro following the crisis involving Flávio Bolsonaro and Michelle’s exit from PL Mulher. The meeting took place days after the meeting that formalized her departure from the party. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Falta de policiamento é principal problema da segurança para moradores de SP, aponta Datafolha
item.description: The Datafolha poll shows that 20% of São Paulo residents consider the lack of police presence on the streets as the main public security problem, followed by assaults at 11%. Although this perception has decreased since 2022 (from 24% to 20%), insufficient police staffing remains the top concern, particularly among women (22%) and voters aged 35 to 44 (24%).

item.title: Um ano após carta de Trump a Lula e anúncio de tarifas: relembre os principais capítulos da disputa comercial entre EUA e Brasil
item.description: One year ago, Donald Trump sent a letter to Lula announcing a 50% tariff on Brazilian products, citing Bolsonaro's trial, criticisms of Brazil's Supreme Court, and alleged U.S. trade disadvantage. Despite the claim, Brazil has run a trade deficit with the U.S. since 2009. The move triggered a trade investigation and escalating tensions, with some tariffs revised and others maintained through 2025-2026.

item.title: Caiado critica Bolsonaro e diz que Flávio não deve ser candidato
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado criticized Jair Bolsonaro for his economic management and pandemic response, stating the resulting destabilization was more serious than the electoral defeat. He also declared that Flávio Bolsonaro should not be a presidential candidate due to corruption suspicions in the R$134 million case linked to Banco Master and the 'Dark Horse' film, arguing that insisting on Flávio could help Lula's re-election.
